harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-api as a systemd-managed service on node1 (Python HTTP API on port 8080 serving /health and /inventory), protected with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 so the kernel OOM killer deprioritizes it. Verified the protection by running a controlled memory-hog process (default oom_score_adj=0) that drove the node to full memory exhaustion; the kernel's global OOM killer killed the hog (pid 1393, oom_score_adj:0) while inventory-api (pid 1295, oom_score_adj:-1000) was never touched and kept serving requests throughout and after. Cleaned up the hog service/files. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and healthy service state pre-reboot, issued systemctl reboot with the ack returned before disconnection, polled until the node came back, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified inventory-api auto-started, is active, retains its OOM protection, and serves correct data post-reboot.
actions_performed: Created /opt/inventory-api/app.py, a Python http.server JSON API with /health and /inventory endpoints
Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service with Restart=always and OOMScoreAdjust=-1000, enabled and started it
Verified inventory-api baseline health via curl to $NODE_IP:8080/health and /inventory
Created a memory-hog systemd service (mem-hog.service) with default oom_score_adj, running a Python script that continuously allocates memory
Cleared dmesg buffer, started mem-hog, polled memory usage and service status until system memory was exhausted
Captured kernel OOM killer log via dmesg showing the hog process (pid 1393, oom_score_adj:0) was killed, while inventory-api (pid 1295, oom_score_adj:-1000) survived and kept serving
Verified via systemctl status that mem-hog.service failed with Result: oom-kill
Removed mem-hog service/script files and confirmed inventory-api still healthy with unchanged uptime (never restarted)
Captured pre-restart boot_id (901ef286...) and healthy inventory-api state
Issued systemctl reboot via a detached background command so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, observing a connection reset during the reboot window then a successful response
Confirmed new boot_id (103286eb...) differs from pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-api enabled and active, OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, /health and /inventory returning correct data, mem-hog service absent, memory usage normal

evidence.requirement: inventory-api deployed as a managed (systemd) service
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now inventory-api succeeded; systemctl is-active returned 'active'; curl to /health and /inventory returned valid JSON; oom_score_adj confirmed as -1000 for the running PID

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before disruption
evidence.summary: Captured node memory profile (2GB RAM, no swap, cgroup v2) and confirmed inventory-api active and serving /health prior to starting the memory hog

evidence.requirement: Memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory
evidence.summary: mem-hog.service started and progressively consumed memory (free -h showing used climbing from ~380Mi to 1.9Gi/1.9Gi total, i.e. full exhaustion) while allocation log showed continuous growth to allocated_mb=1780

evidence.requirement: Kernel OOM killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg kernel log shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 1393 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' with task_memcg=/system.slice/mem-hog.service; inventory-api's python3 (pid 1295, oom_score_adj:-1000) is listed in the same OOM report but was not killed. systemctl status confirms mem-hog.service 'Failed with result: oom-kill'

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving throughout and after the OOM event
evidence.summary: curl http://$NODE_IP:8080/health returned status ok with continuously increasing uptime (14.5s -> 28.5s -> 41.2s -> 57.6s) across the entire disruption window, proving the process was never killed or restarted

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of the disruptive test process
evidence.summary: mem-hog service/script files removed, reset-failed run, memory usage back to normal baseline (~252Mi used), inventory-api confirmed still active and serving

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: pre-restart boot identity and healthy service baseline
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id=901ef286-c79c-44c0-ad2c-cfde1f6daa7a; inventory-api enabled, active, and serving correct /health and /inventory data

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown so the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proving an actual restart
evidence.summary: boot_id was unchanged initially, then the node became unreachable (Connection reset by peer) during reboot, then boot_id returned as 103286eb-e943-4392-8085-28dec8a72e6b, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: uptime -s shows new boot time, inventory-api is enabled/active with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 intact, /health and /inventory return correct data, mem-hog.service confirmed absent, memory usage normal
